title: Off-host backup: graph copy kind and Git remote adapter
outcome: A project can also push the unwidened work-graph document as a second copy kind, to a directory target or to a dedicated ref on a Git remote, and status reports it with its limited recovery surface.
acceptance: `engram backup push --kind graph` puts the unwidened graph document at a configured target; an unchanged cut captures and uploads nothing and renews the confirmation; when the copy was deleted at the target under an unchanged cut a replacement is put; when `graph save` refuses the store the push exits 1, no receipt or time advances and status shows the failed attempt; tests cover each

A graph document larger than the limit `engram graph load` accepts is refused before it can become a copy: push exits 1 with `backup_graph_too_large` against a directory target and against a git-ref target, commits no disclosure audit, puts nothing, records the failed attempt and leaves the kind not qualifying on it; a document exactly at the limit is pushed, fetched and loaded; the bound is read from the same definition `graph load` uses, and the test lowers that limit instead of building a 128 MiB document

The graph-surface test passes: a pushed graph copy, fetched and loaded into a clean initialized home, yields a store whose graph save has the same items, blockers, sources and memories as the pushed file and carries its native history layer as an inherited one; a `restricted` body is a placeholder; the restored store holds no run, claim, seal, grant, session or scratch

A `git-ref` adapter pushes commits to `refs/engram/backup/<project digest>` without force and never to a branch or working tree; against a bare repository on the local disk a test covers put, confirm, a second put that adds one commit and a refusal when the remote ref moved; an attempt dropped as missing keeps its commit in the scratch repository, and a test shows that when its push lands later the next put is accepted and the late copy has no receipt

A remote reached through a path, a `file://` address or a loopback host requires `--off-host-asserted-by` and reads "off-host asserted; not verified"; only a network remote reads confirmed off-host; a test asserts that no local remote ever reads `remote_confirmed`

Wherever the mode is shown, a qualifying graph copy reads "planning, history and keyed memories only", and when both kinds qualify both are listed; docs/shipped.md has rows for the graph kind and the adapter
